title: Law firm or accountants

fields.label: Where you are
fields.help: Town or city, and whether you see clients in person.

fields.label: Regulation
fields.help: Who regulates you and your number, exactly as it must appear (e.g. SRA No. 123456, ICAEW, ACCA).

fields.label: What you do
fields.help: Your areas of work and the situations clients come to you with, with typical fees and how long things take.

fields.label: Fixed fees
fields.help: Your headline fixed fees and what's included. Say if prices are plus VAT.

fields.label: Your people
fields.help: Two to four people: name, role, what they handle, a line about them.

fields.label: How you work
fields.help: Free first call? How quickly you reply? Phone, video or in person?

fields.label: A typical matter
fields.help: Optional: one typical job from start to finish (a house purchase, a tax return, a settlement agreement) so we can show it step by step.

fields.label: Brand colour
fields.help: Optional: a name or hex code.

writerNotes: The hero works one example matter on a desk as you scroll: a first note, papers arriving, papers sorted into tabbed folders, a close read with highlights and numbered flags, an advice memo typed out, then a signature and a stamp. stages are those six steps, each a short name, a caption and the day count since the matter opened. Make it the brief's typical matter (a house purchase, a tax return, a settlement agreement); for accountants the folders are like Income, Expenses, Receipts, Bank and the stamp says Filed.

matter: the example's reference (letters from the firm's name, a dash, digits), how many points the close read flags (1-3, matching the fourth caption), its fixed fee as shown on the ledger, the stamp word, 3-5 folder labels, and the memo's title and 2-4 short points (each under 44 characters) that answer the flags.

contact.reg is the regulatory line exactly as the brief gives it; never invent a regulator or a number. If the brief gives none, write that the firm's regulatory details are available on request and list it in _assumed.

guide.areas: the brief's areas (two to five), each with one to four situations: fee [low, high] (equal if fixed), how long it takes, who handles it (exactly a name from people.list), two to four plain steps, and what to have ready. Use the brief's fees; if a range is missing, list it in _assumed.
fees: one to four headline fixed fees with from: true if it is a starting price, and what's included. fees.vat is the VAT or sales tax rate in percent, 0 if prices are shown without one.
people.list: two to four people from the brief, never invented. consult.how lists, in order, phone, video, in person (only those offered); consult.promises are two to four things the brief promises.
hero.title and hero.titleEm are a short two-part headline (four lines at most on a desktop). theme.accent is the firm's colour, dark enough for white button text; theme.wordmarkFit is always "fit".
business.name is set to exactly the firm's name in the brief and cannot be changed; brand.name is how it appears in the nav and footer.
